[VERIFIED_FACT_CARD]
- meaning: You chose the 10 kWe fission rover: about 17 h of range to move 6,000 kg (driving needs ~13.44 kWe).
- real history: On Apollo 15, 16 and 17 astronauts drove the Lunar Roving Vehicle on non-rechargeable batteries, with one rule: never drive farther than they could walk back if the rover failed.
- source: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (LRV)
- simple analogy: It is like a car with a full tank: you can go far and come back. With little energy, every kilometre out is one you must be able to return.
- tone: good

[CADET_ANSWER] Because if the rover breaks down you must be able to walk back before the suit's oxygen runs out.
